ras-nungwi-lighthouse.hook: Unguja's oldest lighthouse, a white stone tower lit in 1926 at the island's northern point.
ras-nungwi-lighthouse.why: Ras Nungwi, which old charts call Hog Point, is the northern tip of Unguja, and a light has marked it since the 1880s. The tower there now is a white square stone tower in three stages, built in 1926: 14 metres tall with a focal height of 18 metres, and its white flash reaches 13 nautical miles. The Zanzibar Ports Corporation still runs it as a working light, so you see it from outside only.

kendwa-beach.hook: A west-facing beach on Unguja where the sea stays close at low tide, so you can swim most of the day.
kendwa-beach.why: Along most of Zanzibar's east and south-east coast the sea goes out a long way at low tide and you plan swims around the tide table. Kendwa, on the north-west coast, shelves quickly, so the water is deep enough to swim in for most of the day whatever the tide is doing. It also faces west, so you can stay in the water until the sun goes down.
facts: Kendwa is less affected by tides than most Zanzibar beaches because the water deepens quickly (Easy Travel / Jaynevy Tours).

mkokotoni.hook: The fish landing at Mkokotoni, on Unguja's north-west coast, directly across the water from Tumbatu.
mkokotoni.why: Mkokotoni is the north-west coast town where boats bring their catch ashore and local buyers, men and women, haggle over it on the spot, a market for people who live here rather than a sight laid on for visitors. It faces Tumbatu across a narrow channel, and the island's largest old mosque ruin stands on the shore looking back at it. Go early and bring Tanzanian shillings in small notes.

mangapwani-cave.hook: A coral cave with a freshwater pool, and nearby a rock-cut cell used to hold slaves after abolition.
mangapwani-cave.why: Two sites on the same coast north of Stone Town. The coral cave is a natural cavern with a narrow entrance and a pool of fresh water at the bottom. A few kilometres on is a square cell cut into the coral rock and roofed over around 1880, seven years after the 1873 treaty that banned the slave trade, and used to hold captives illegally until about 1905. Entry is roughly US$5.
